transcript.text: Hi, my Hotpoint Aquarius dryer is taking forever to dry and the top gets really hot. Model is TCM580GUK if that helps

The combination of very slow drying and a very hot top most often points to restricted airflow: fluff in the door filter, a blocked condenser/lower filter, or a squashed/blocked vent hose. The dryer can still make heat, but cannot move it away properly, so drying takes much longer and the casing gets hotter. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Remove and clean the door fluff filter thoroughly. A filter can look clear but have a film of lint and conditioner residue restricting air. 2. Check behind the lower front flap. If there is a removable condenser, rinse fluff from it under the tap and let it drip-dry before refitting. If it has filters instead, clean those as directed on the flap. Heavy fluff there strongly supports an airflow cause. 3. Check any hose at the back runs freely to its outlet: no kinks, crushing or fluff blockage. If it is vented outside, make sure the outside grille opens and is clear. 4. For the next load, use a normal heat programme and keep the drum no more than about two-thirds full; laundry that went in poorly spun will also take much longer. If the filters and air path are clean but it still becomes excessively hot or drying remains poor, the next possibilities are the blower fan not moving enough air, or a thermostat/thermal cut-out issue. That is better checked by an engineer rather than replacing parts blindly. If there is a burning-lint smell, smoke, scorching, or it cuts out when hot, stop using it and leave it unplugged until it has been checked.

Thank you. The door filter had a thick layer of fluff on it, I must admit I sometimes forget to clean it. The condenser at the front had lint packed on the fins, and it looks much cleaner after a rinse. I'm not sure about any hose at the back. The loads are normal size from a 1400 spin washer. I should also say that I often run the dryer while I'm out at work, so is that a concern given how hot the top gets?

Yes — I would stop running it while you are out, at least until it has completed a successful supervised test after the cleaning. A dryer’s casing can become warm in normal use, but a top that feels really hot alongside slow drying is not something to leave unattended, particularly when the airflow had been heavily restricted by lint. The packed door filter and condenser are a strong explanation for both symptoms, and cleaning them may well cure it. Once the condenser is fully drip-dry and securely refitted: 1. Run a normal heat programme while you are at home, with a normal load.
2. Check it periodically rather than leaving it overnight or unattended. Stop and unplug it if there is a burning smell, smoke, scorching, unusual noise, or it becomes too hot to comfortably keep a hand on.
3. If drying is now back to normal and the top is only warm rather than excessively hot, the blockage was the likely cause. Clean the door filter after every load and the condenser regularly. If it is still taking a long time or the top is still excessively hot after this clean-out, do not keep using it unattended; an engineer should check the internal airflow/fan and the temperature-control parts.
[Safety panel] Clean the lint filter after every load — a build-up of fluff is a fire risk and restricts airflow. Don't run the dryer overnight or while you're out.

candidates: Restricted airflow from lint build-up or a blocked/kinked vent path (high)
Thermostat or thermal cut-out problem after airflow restriction (low)

reading.symptom: taking a long time to dry; top gets very hot

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Hotpoint; model TCM580GUK.
The fault they reported is: "taking a long time to dry; top gets very hot". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

candidates: Restricted airflow from the heavily blocked fluff filter and condenser (high)
Internal fan, ducting or temperature-control fault if poor drying/overheating continues after cleaning (low)
